F1_high_declared_reference_functional_co.statement: The artifact scores `ref` as the exact field sampled at FE element isoparametric centres, but its own `reference_functional` string declares 'exact Lame field volume-averaged over the same radial layer (lame_layer_average)'. The two differ by 7.5% (hex20 sigma_r inner: declared -877083 vs scored -811263) and by 13.3% (hex8: -659239 vs -747124). Scored against the declared functional, the selected hex20 ladder is 8.03% on sigma_r_inner (>5%), i.e. the case does NOT meet the pool tolerance, and the hex8 baseline (4.10%) would have passed.

F2_high_layer_bounds_are_half_layers.statement: `probe_metrics` derives layer bounds from torch.unique(node radii); for HEX20 the unique radii include edge-midside nodes (8.333, 9.667 ...), so the advertised exact `layer_integrals` are integrated over half-layers ([8,8.333] and [9.667,10]) instead of the true element layers ([8,8.667] and [9.333,10]). Verified on the delivered mesh (_mesh(6,3,2): node radii = 8.0, 8.333, 8.667, 9.0, 9.333, 9.667, 10.0; last-ring element-centre radii 9.549-9.628, i.e. elements span [9.333,10]).
F2_high_layer_bounds_are_half_layers.impact: the artifact's 'independent global check' is computed on the wrong intervals and therefore cannot detect the 8.03% error

F3_medium_probe_locations_biassed_inward.statement: Stress probes are evaluated at the isoparametric centre (xi=eta=zeta=0) of curved HEX20 bricks. Measured on the delivered mesh: inner ring centres 8.224-8.298 m, outer ring centres 9.549-9.628 m, i.e. the outer-ring sample sits ~0.08 m inside the element volume centroid (~9.68 m). For sigma_r ~ 1/r^3 this location bias alone shifts the layer value by ~2-3%, so `got` is not a volume average of the FE field either.
